Thinking Geographically: Human geography
The study of how people shape and are shaped by places
Absolute location
A precise position given by coordinates
Relative location
A position described in relation to other places
Place
The physical and human characteristics that make a location distinctive
Region
An area unified by one or more shared characteristics
Formal region
A region with a measurable shared trait, such as a language area
Functional region
A region organised around a node, such as a metro delivery zone
Perceptual region
A region defined by people's beliefs, such as the American South
Scale of analysis
The level, from local to global, at which data is examined
Map projection
A method of representing a curved Earth on a flat surface
Mercator projection
A projection preserving direction but distorting high-latitude area
Choropleth map
A map using shading to show values by area
Cartogram
A map that sizes areas by a variable rather than land area
Geographic information system
Software layering spatial data for analysis
Remote sensing
Collecting data about Earth from satellites or aircraft
Distance decay
Interaction weakening as distance between places increases
Time-space compression
Technology reducing the effective distance between places
Spatial diffusion
The spread of a phenomenon across space over time
Environmental determinism
The discredited idea that environment dictates culture
Possibilism
The view that environment sets limits but people choose responses
Population and Migration Patterns and Pr: Population density
The number of people per unit of area
Arithmetic density
Total population divided by total land area
Physiological density
Population divided by arable land area
Agricultural density
Number of farmers per unit of arable land
Carrying capacity
The population an environment can sustainably support
Crude birth rate
Live births per thousand people per year
Total fertility rate
The average number of children a woman bears in her lifetime
Rate of natural increase
Birth rate minus death rate, excluding migration
Doubling time
The years required for a population to double at its current rate
Demographic transition model
A five-stage model of birth and death rate change with development
Stage two of demographic transition
Death rates fall sharply while birth rates stay high
Stage four of demographic transition
Low birth and death rates producing near-zero growth
Population pyramid
A graph of population by age and sex
Dependency ratio
The ratio of dependents to working-age population
Malthusian theory
The claim that population outgrows food supply
Epidemiological transition
The shift in leading causes of death as societies develop
Pronatalist policy
A policy encouraging higher birth rates
Antinatalist policy
A policy discouraging births to slow growth
Push factor
A negative condition driving people to leave a place
Pull factor
A positive condition attracting people to a place
Ravenstein's laws of migration
Generalisations that most migrants move short distances for economic reasons
Voluntary versus forced migration
Chosen relocation versus movement under compulsion
Refugee
A person fleeing across a border due to well-founded fear of persecution
Internally displaced person
Someone forced from home who remains within their own country
Chain migration
Migrants following relatives or countrymen to a destination
Remittance
Money migrants send home to family
Guest worker
A migrant admitted temporarily to fill labour shortages
Cultural Patterns and Processes: Culture
The shared practices, beliefs, and material traits of a group
Cultural trait
A single element of culture, such as a food or gesture
Cultural landscape
The visible imprint of human activity on the land
Folk culture
Traditional practices of small, homogeneous, often rural groups
Popular culture
Widespread practices spread rapidly through mass media
Cultural hearth
The place where a cultural trait originates
Relocation diffusion
Spread carried by people physically moving
Expansion diffusion
Spread outward from a hearth while remaining at the source
Hierarchical diffusion
Spread from larger or more powerful places to smaller ones
Contagious diffusion
Rapid spread through direct contact across a population
Stimulus diffusion
The underlying idea spreading even when the specific form does not
Acculturation
Adopting traits of another culture while keeping one's own
Assimilation
Fully absorbing into another culture and losing the original
Syncretism
The blending of two cultural traditions into something new
Language family
A group of languages descended from a common ancestor
Lingua franca
A common language adopted for communication between groups
Creole language
A stable language developed from a pidgin
Universalizing religion
A religion seeking converts worldwide, such as Christianity or Islam
Ethnic religion
A religion tied to a particular people and place, such as Hinduism
Ethnic enclave
A neighbourhood dominated by one ethnic group
Cultural relativism
Judging a culture by its own standards
Placelessness
The loss of distinctive local character to global uniformity
Political Patterns and Processes: State
A politically organised territory with sovereignty and permanent population
Nation
A group sharing culture, language, or identity
Nation-state
A state whose borders roughly match a single nation
Stateless nation
A people without a sovereign state of their own
Multinational state
A state containing more than one nation
Sovereignty
A state's authority to govern itself without outside interference
Colonialism
One power establishing settlements and control in a foreign territory
Imperialism
Extending a state's power over others by force or influence
Berlin Conference
The 1884 meeting that partitioned Africa among European powers
Boundary types
Geometric, physical, and cultural lines dividing territories
Antecedent boundary
A boundary drawn before an area was heavily settled
Subsequent boundary
A boundary drawn after settlement, following cultural divisions
Superimposed boundary
A boundary forced on an area, ignoring existing culture
Relic boundary
A former boundary still visible in the landscape
Landlocked state
A state without direct access to the ocean
Compact state
A state whose distance from centre to edge varies little
Elongated state
A long, narrow state facing internal communication challenges
Fragmented state
A state made of discontinuous pieces of territory
Perforated state
A state completely surrounding another state
Unitary state
A state concentrating power in the central government
Federal state
A state distributing power among regional units
Devolution
The transfer of power from central government to regions
Centrifugal force
A force pulling a state apart
Centripetal force
A force binding a state together
Supranational organization
An alliance of states pooling some sovereignty, such as the EU
Balkanization
The fragmentation of a region into hostile smaller units
Agriculture and Rural Land-Use Patterns: Agriculture
The deliberate cultivation of plants and raising of animals
First agricultural revolution
The Neolithic shift from foraging to domestication
Second agricultural revolution
Mechanisation and improved yields alongside industrialisation
Green Revolution
Twentieth-century high-yield seeds, fertiliser, and irrigation
Subsistence agriculture
Farming primarily to feed the farmer's own household
Commercial agriculture
Farming primarily for sale in the market
Intensive agriculture
High inputs of labour or capital on a small area
Extensive agriculture
Low inputs spread over a large area, such as ranching
Shifting cultivation
Clearing and farming a plot then moving on as fertility falls
Slash-and-burn
Clearing land by cutting and burning vegetation
Pastoral nomadism
Herding livestock across seasonal grazing land
Transhumance
Seasonal movement of livestock between highland and lowland pasture
Plantation agriculture
Large commercial farms in tropical regions growing a single cash crop
Monoculture
Growing one crop repeatedly over a large area
Von Thunen model
A model predicting land use rings based on transport cost and rent
Bid-rent theory
Land value declining with distance from a market centre
Township and range system
A grid survey producing square land parcels in the US interior
Metes and bounds
A survey system using natural features to define parcels
Agribusiness
The corporate integration of farming with processing and distribution
Food desert
An area with limited access to affordable fresh food
Sustainable agriculture
Farming methods preserving soil, water, and long-term yield
Desertification
The degradation of productive land into desert conditions
Cities and Urban Land-Use Patterns: Urbanization
The growing concentration of population in cities
Site and situation
A city's physical setting versus its relative position and connections
Megacity
A city with more than ten million residents
Metacity
A city exceeding twenty million residents
World city
A city exerting global economic and cultural influence
Primate city
A city more than twice the size of the next largest in a country
Rank-size rule
The pattern where the nth city is one nth the size of the largest
Central place theory
Christaller's model explaining the spacing and size of settlements
Range and threshold
The maximum distance customers travel versus the minimum market needed
Gravity model
A prediction that interaction rises with size and falls with distance
Concentric zone model
Burgess's model of rings expanding from a central business district
Sector model
Hoyt's model of land use developing in wedges along transport lines
Multiple nuclei model
Harris and Ullman's model of several specialised centres
Galactic city model
A model of edge cities linked by beltways around a weakened core
Central business district
The commercial and often historic core of a city
Suburbanization
The outward growth of residential areas beyond the city core
Urban sprawl
Low-density expansion consuming land at the urban fringe
Smart growth
Planning that concentrates development and preserves open space
New urbanism
Design promoting walkability, mixed use, and traditional neighbourhoods
Gentrification
Wealthier residents moving into and transforming a lower-income area
Redlining
The discriminatory denial of loans in certain neighbourhoods
Blockbusting
Provoking panic selling by exploiting racial fear
Urban heat island
Cities being warmer than surrounding rural areas
Squatter settlement
Informal housing built on land the residents do not own
Zoning
Regulation designating permitted land uses in an area
Industrial and Economic Development Patt: The shift to machine production beginning in eighteenth-century Britain
Knowledge-based activity such as research and information processing
The highest-level decision making in government and business
Locating industry to minimise transport, labour, and agglomeration costs
An industry locating near raw materials because inputs weigh more
An industry locating near markets because output weighs more
Firms clustering to share suppliers, labour, and infrastructure
The decline of manufacturing in a formerly industrial region
Contracting work externally versus relocating it abroad
An area with relaxed rules to attract foreign investment
A location where goods transfer between transport modes
A common measure of average national income
A composite of income, education, and life expectancy
A measure of disparity in health, empowerment, and labour
A five-stage model from traditional society to mass consumption
A model dividing the world into core, periphery, and semi-periphery
The view that poor countries remain poor because of exploitative ties
Small loans supporting entrepreneurship in low-income areas
Free-market reforms reducing state economic intervention
Meeting present needs without compromising future generations
Travel designed to support conservation and local communities
